one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-23 to 2026-11-22 holds no Meta earnings. Scheduled: FOMC 27-28 Oct; Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon Q3 calls 28-30 Oct with the first numeric 2027 capex guides (the AI-capex file expects them; high guides have hit META on capex-angst days, e.g. -3.3% on 14 Oct when Guggenheim lifted its 2027 Meta capex to $225B); Nvidia results around 19 Nov; autumn California state youth bellwether trials; possible board notice of the Class C record date (charter effective 19 Jan 2027, so no split mechanics in the window). Short-horizon pattern: META fell after three straight prints (Oct-25, Jul-26 ~-10%, Oct-26 -8% after a beat) and recovered over the next months each time, but that is a small sample, so we keep only a ~0.5% upward tilt. Spread: monthly s.d. ~12% (43%/3.5) as a mix of an 85% normal regime (10.5%) and a 15% event regime (19%) for the read-across from peer capex guides and trial news.

META's own history supports it: it has traded below the mega-cap median in most of 2022-2026 (18-23x forward in 2026). We do not assume the discount closes.

thesis_break_reason: $470 (-27%, below the $520 52-week low) is about 14x our NTM EPS, a level META only reached in the 2022 capex/ad-recession scare. Trading there would most likely mean the earnings path is broken (price per ad falling y/y, or a 2027 capex guide above ~$250B with no revenue lift) or a legal/regulatory hit far above the AG settlement, rather than ordinary 43%-vol noise; it matches our bear-scenario value.

reasoning: All per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share: today's Class A share plus the one Class C share it receives in the dividend payable after the 2027-01-19 charter date; enterprise value is unchanged by it. Evidence: Q3-26 revenue +26% (impressions +10%, price +14%), Q4 guide $73-76B; Meta has finished 2-4% above the revenue guide midpoint in each of the last four quarters, so we sit at the top ($76.1B). FY2026 expenses land at the $177B guide midpoint (incl. $12.3B legal charges). The stock fell ~8% after a beat on the Class C news and capex fears, the third negative print reaction in a row, after a ~25% September rally on the Muse launch; consensus FY2027 EPS is $33.92. Driver build: ads +19% in 2027 and +14% in 2028; FoA margin falls from ~44% ex-charges to 38% and 35.5% because D&A climbs from $28B to ~$71B on capex of $141B/$205B/$252B (AI-file base, with Meta's record of exceeding first capex guides by 16-21% in up-years); 2027 EPS ~$31.7 is ~6% below consensus for that reason. Valuation: 21x NTM P/E (15% below the peer median, mid of META's 2026 range of 18-23x) and a SOTP with FoA at 16x EBIT and RL on its own give a research target (12m) of $725. Base rates: META's own 12-month return s.d. is ~0.42 and its post-drawdown history is very strong, but survivor-biased; Kalshi prices a 20% chance of a 2027 recession and META's price per ad fell 18% y/y in 2022, which sets the bear weight. Prediction markets on META itself (Polymarket via Polyguana) are short-dated and thin, so they carry no weight. Ladder: three lognormals at the engine's bear ($477, 25%, s.d. 0.27) and bull ($939, 25%, s.d. 0.22) and a base shaded from $725 to $705 toward price-plus-drift ($700) because research targets have overshot; median ~$702, mean ~$725, P(above today) 0.60. Not driver-linked: the investments adjustment (+$24.5B) and the stated net debt at horizon. Research was limited by blocked pages (S&P/Visible Alpha previews, Nasdaq), and no option data was used.

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led set (6 drivers: impressions, price per ad, FoA other revenue, FoA margin, RL revenue, RL loss) reproduces FY2025 revenue exactly; driven share 100%. Value carried by two legs: a sum of the parts (55%: FoA at 16x NTM EV/EBIT, Reality Labs on its own as -3.5x after-tax loss, both driver-linked) and a 21x NTM GAAP P/E on the build's own EPS (45%). Non-marketable investments added as an adjustment on both legs. No DCF leg (not a neocloud). Capex follows the AI-capex file base and only affects D&A and net debt.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) RL valued at -3.5x after-tax loss (-$41B) instead of being capitalised at the full multiple; moving to the P/E-implied treatment would lower the SOTP leg by ~$79/share (>5%). (2) Net debt at horizon stated directly ($72B) because the engine bridge omits the SBC add-back and the net-share-settlement cash. (3) Per-share values are per CURRENT pre-split share (Class A + the Class C dividend share). fair_value.value equals the engine base horizon value.
